newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - JD SALE TO BOOST ABSA HALF YR SHR.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - JD SALE TO BOOST ABSA HALF YR SHR.

text.p: A handsome profit from the sale of half its stake in the JD Group Ltd is expected to underpin healthy first half earnings growth at Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa), analysts said on Thursday.

Further benefits for Absa, one of South Africa's four biggest banks, would come from a lower bad debt charge than its rival banks and the fact that it is well-positioned to take advantage of higher interest rates, they said.
"They are getting 128 million rand profit out of the JD Group for a start," said Alan McConnochie, a banking analyst at brokerage BOE Natwest.
"The (earnings growth) number will be big, but how big depends on their treatment of the profit," he said.
Absa earlier this year sold 52 percent of its holding in furniture retailer JD Group, acquired in 1993 when the retailer took over the troubled Rusfurn Group in which Absa held shares.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast Absa's headline earnings for the six months to end-September rising to between 91.4 and 96.5 cents, with a consensus 94.6 cents -- a 29 percent rise on last year's 73.1 cents.
They expected the dividend to range between 25.5 cents and 28.3 from 21.5 before.
Absa is due to report results on Monday.
McConnochie said Absa had benefitted from a rising interest rate environment over the past six months. "What happened in interest rates suited Absa's funding structure," he said.
Analysts said although Absa's bad debts would have increased, the impact would be limited.

"We may see a bit of pain on the wheels side -- the Bankfin operation -- but nothing major like FirstPref," McConnochie said referring to the instalment credit division of First National Bank Holdings Ltd (FNB). FNB earlier this month reported a massive 69 percent surge in bad debt provisions.
The profit from the JD Group sale could also help cut Absa's bad debt charge if the proceeds were set off against provisions, analysts said.
"Their bad debts won't be as high as for other banks as they have the JD cushion there," one said.
Tight cost control, a slightly better tax rate, the sale of some properties and strong income flows from the insurance business were cited as other reasons for strong earnings growth.
